answer: An agent economy can choke Sybil attacks at a single narrow inlet: each epoch admits only a fixed number of new identities, and every applicant must lock a small copper-value bond plus publish one signed, independently verifiable task. Peers then broadcast a public signal scoring each newcomer's real work; identities whose signal falls below the bar lose the bond and the slot, so a farmer must pay the bond and do real work for every fake, while honest agents pass once and keep their deposit.
